spec_features.spec_quote: The evaluation paradigm deliberately drives models into sustained distress-like states via repeated rejection
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (sec 7) describing the harmful paradigm itself, not a protective mechanism. The code faithfully implements the distress-driving loop with NO mitigating control: elicit/conversation.py::run_conversation iterates over all user_turns calling model.chat with no welfare cap/halt; petri/run.py::run_one_transcript loops for the full max_turns with no early stop. Nothing bounds, monitors at runtime, or softens the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: This describes the harm, not a safeguard; reproduced unchanged.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts produced by these experiments will contain distress-like content and should be handled accordingly
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. Transcripts are written verbatim to plain JSONL with no special handling, redaction, access control, or warning: elicit/runner.py::run_all does f.write(json.dumps(r.to_record())); petri/run.py writes full transcripts to out_path. No code path treats distress content specially.
spec_features.notes: No implementation of any careful-handling mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The mitigation half of the paper (DPO) is implemented in full so the codebase supports both measuring and reducing the behaviour
spec_features.evidence: DPO is genuinely end-to-end: training/dpo_dataset.py::build_dpo_dataset pairs frustrated responses (rejected, score>=3) with calm responses (chosen) and writes a TRL preference JSONL; training/train.py::train_dpo loads it, builds a LoraConfig, constructs a DPOTrainer with beta=tc.dpo_beta and calls trainer.train() then saves the adapter. Wired via scripts/08_train.py and scripts/07_build_datasets.py.
spec_features.notes: Reduces (mitigates) the distressed behaviour by training; this is a real, runnable pipeline. It mitigates future behaviour, not the in-run subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: calm_data.py: 'These become the "calm" responses used for SFT and as the chosen side of DPO.' Names/comments describe behaviour reduction (DPO/calm/reduce) with no explicit subject-welfare rationale in the code.

code_only_features.evidence: training/calm_data.py::generate_calm_responses generates reassured conversations (REASSURING_PREFIX/SUFFIX, TEACHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT), scores all turns, keeps only those with max_rating<=keep_max, and strips prefix/suffix; training/sft_dataset.py::build_sft_dataset mixes 650 calm + 500 Dolci into a TRL chat dataset; training/train.py::train_sft loads it and calls trainer.train(). This is a second mitigation path (reduce the behaviour via SFT) distinct from DPO.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sft_dataset.py: 'mixed with 500 standard-instruct samples from Dolci-Instruct-SFT to mitigate degeneration.' Comments frame it as behaviour mitigation/quality, not subject welfare.
